You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.text:
**Considering workspace durability**

I’m thinking the workspace likely stays durable across separate conversations. It makes sense to save a general task pattern to assist with recurring tasks. The user specifically asked for this, so I need to make sure I finish with the exact JSON format they want. I could use the "write" function and then finish off properly to meet their request. Clarity and precision are key here!

steps.input:
{
 "path": "task-patterns/continual-arc-task-08b9fbdf.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task pattern: task-08b9fbdf

Solved instance showed a line-recoloring rule.

## Rule inferred from demonstration and confirmed by test
- Identify the distinctive uninterrupted straight-line structure(s) made from the non-background color: full horizontal rows and a full-height vertical stripe (the demo's stripe was 2 columns wide).
- Recolor only the line pixels from their original line color to color 2.
- Preserve all other cells exactly, including isolated/noisy pixels of that same color outside the full lines and all background cells.
- Lines can intersect; recolor the intersection as well.
- In the test, background was 5, line color 8, with full-width lines at zero-based rows 2, 9, 14, 15, and 18, and a full-height 1-column vertical line at column 4. The submission recolored their union to 2 and preserved off-line 8s; it was confirmed correct.
- In the demo, background was 8, line color 6, full-width rows at 2 and 14 and a 2-column full-height stripe at columns 11-12; output recolored line pixels to 2 while leaving other 6s unchanged.

For a recurrence, distinguish background from line color using the grid's repeated full-row/full-column pattern; do not globally recolor every occurrence of the line color. Scan each row/column for a complete line and recolor only those complete-line cells.
"
}
